name: Ephrath
overview: Ephrath is a female biblical figure known primarily as the second wife of Chelubai (Caleb) according to 1 Chronicles 2:19. There is no record of her tribal affiliation or additional notes beyond this relationship. Her mention is brief but significant in the genealogical context of Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ephrath means "fruitful land," reflecting a Hebrew proper name with agricultural connotations. This meaning is not indicated as being divinely given but provides insight into the cultural background of her identity as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ephrath as the wife of Chelubai (Caleb), making her part of his family line. No other family relationships are explicitly documented beyond this marital connection in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ephrath's significance lies in her role within the genealogical records of Israel, linking her to the lineage of Caleb, a notable figure in the Old Testament. Her mention as a second wife highlights the complexities of family structures in biblical times and contributes to the understanding of Israel's tribal and familial history as preserved in 1 Chronicles.
